note: The measurements of Tables 35/36 are transcribed as ranges and means; in Table 36 the ranges of the "left mandible length" and "pronotum length" rows are misaligned with their labels in the PDF text extraction, so their values are not recorded and the rest is transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with the darkest wings among the West Indian species of the genus, especially dark at the wing base (most obvious when folded over the abdomen), and the wings are also very short and narrow (mean 6.67 mm, 6.25—7.24 mm); C. parvifrons and C. cryptognathus have wings of similar size but far paler than this species. Soldier most similar to C. cylindroceps, differing in the longer mandibles, the head capsule not cylindrical, and the wrinkles of the head capsule and frons far deeper (the wrinkles of the anterior 1/3—1/2 are brain-like). A rare forest-dwelling species. Distribution: Trinidad and Tobago in the Lesser Antilles, West Indies (Tobago a new record), unknown elsewhere. Type specimen data in Bacchus 1987.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Whole body light brown; sclerotized veins brown, wing membrane smoky, light brown; head light brown to brown, with a dark transverse band between the compound eyes; a brown chevron mark distinct on the forewing scale; pronotum light brown to brown; abdominal tergites brown, sternites, labrum and antennae light brown; femora whitish, tibiae and other distal parts light brown. Head oval, cranial sutures weak; compound eyes medium-sized, nearly oval, straight along the edge of the ocellus and the antennal socket; ocelli medium-sized, oval, touching the compound eye. Antennae 14 or 15-segmented, the two about equally frequent, segment formula variable, often 2=3=4=5. Pronotum nearly square, distinctly narrower than the head width at the compound eyes; anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin very slightly concave, sides slightly convex. Forewing radius reaching the wing margin at 1/3 of the wing length from the wing suture; radial sector with 5—7 branches. With arolia. Table 35 measurements (n=9♀, 6♂, 2 colonies): head length including the labrum 1.03—1.18 mm (mean 1.10), head to postclypeus 0.80—0.92 (0.86), head width (maximum at the compound eyes) 0.85—0.93 (0.90), long diameter of the compound eye 0.28—0.32 (0.30), minimum distance from the compound eye to the posterior margin of the head 0.08—0.12 (0.11), ocellus diameter 0.10—0.11 (0.11), pronotum length 0.52—0.60 (0.58), width 0.75—0.83 (0.81), body length with wings 7.95—9.23 (8.64), body length without wings 4.12—4.97 (4.50), forewing length 6.25—7.24 (6.67), maximum width 1.58—1.81 (1.70).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In dorsal view the anterior 1/3—1/2 of the head is almost black, becoming ferruginous posteriorly; in lateral view the anterior 1/3 is almost black, turning ferruginous posteriorly, with a pale yellow stripe along the occipital foramen. Mandibles dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum chestnut brown, the rest orange-yellow. Head nearly square in dorsal view, with a slight but distinct constriction at the eye spots; sides slightly convex, posterior margin slightly convex or nearly straight. The wrinkles of the anterior 1/3—1/2 of the head are characteristically brain-like. The anterior margin of the frontal shield is shallowly incised and double-convex in outline; the surface of the shield is continuous with the vertex and frons, without a boundary. The frontal depression varies from slight to very shallow, and the wrinkles of the whole frontal surface agree with those of the anterior head capsule; the frontal surface forms 90° with the vertex surface; the dorsal margin of the vertex is distinctly concave. Labrum small, triangular, the tip slightly swollen. Frontal horns very short, rounded, continuous with the frontal shield, the surface wrinkles agreeing with those of the frontal surface. Genal horns short, conical, granular on the surface; the axes of the two genal horns diverge outwards. The genal and frontal horns are very close together; in dorsal view the genal horns are not completely hidden by the frontal horns. Mandibles of medium length, slightly sickle-shaped, often slightly swollen at the base, the dentition very short; in lateral view the mandibles project almost horizontally. Eye spots oval and small, or very small with an indistinct outline. Antennae 11—13-segmented, mostly 11 or 13, segment formula variable, often 2>3<4=5. Pronotum broadly shield-shaped, anterior margin shallowly incised and with an additional small, rather deep median notch, sides slightly convex or nearly parallel and slightly contracting backwards, posterior corners broadly rounded, posterior margin straight; the anterior margin shallowly and distinctly wavy. Table 36 measurements (n=15, 4 colonies): head including the mandible tips 1.46—1.59 mm (mean 1.53), head including the frontal horns 1.18—1.30 (1.25), width of the frontal shield 1.00—1.10 (1.07), outer distance between the frontal horns 0.78—0.85 (0.82), head width 0.82—0.92 (0.87), head height (without postmentum) 0.90—1.03 (0.98), pronotum width 0.64—0.80 (0.73), total length 2.97—3.86 (3.46).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: All the material measured here consists of soldiers and alates: Trinidad, Mt. Tabor, foot of St. Benedict Monastery, 10°39.83′N, 61°23.93′W, 1996-v-26, collected by JK (TT85, TT86); Tobago, Anse Brisant Bay trail, 11°18.55′N, 60°31.64′W, 1996-v-31 (TT0557); Tobago, Roxborough road, 11°16.02′N, 60°35.15′W, 1996-v-31 (TT577).
